messages.author: 4958238606a33394
messages.subject: trouble with ggplot
parts:
Hi, I have some trouble to get ggplot working on two UNIX boxes, each
coming back with a different error.

One unix box R2.8.1:

> library(reshape, lib.loc="~/R/myRLibs")
> library(plyr, lib.loc="~/R/myRLibs")
> library(proto, lib.loc="~/R/myRLibs")
> library(ggplot2, lib.loc="~/R/myRLibs")
> qplot(rnorm(100),rnorm(100))
Error in function (..., na.last = TRUE, decreasing = FALSE) :
unimplemented type 'list' in 'orderVector1'

The other unix box R2.11.0:

Error in get("make_aesthetics", env = x, inherits = TRUE)(x, ...) :
could not find function "empty"

In reading another thread, looks like I should upgrade the plyr
library. I actually reinstalled a fresh copy of the reshape, plyr,
ggplot2 packages under a local library ~/R/myRLibs and loaded them
from there by library(plyr,lib.loc="~/R/myRLibs") etc.

Here are the libraries in that directory:

> library(lib.loc="~/R/myRLibs")
Packages in library '~/R/myRLibs':

colorspace Color Space Manipulation
digest Create cryptographic hash digests of R objects
ggplot2 An implementation of the Grammar of Graphics
glpk GNU Linear Programming Kit
iterators Iterator construct for R
itertools Iterator Tools
plyr Tools for splitting, applying and combining
data
proto Prototype object-based programming
RColorBrewer ColorBrewer palettes
reshape Flexibly reshape data.


Can somebody help?

Thanks

Shuping

Hi:

FWIW, your example worked for me (session info below). Considering how old your first box's version of R happens to be, perhaps you could try

d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), y = rnorm(100))
qplot(x, y, data = d)

I seem to recall that ggplot2 prefers data frames as input, despite my success above.

OK I am now able to get qplot working, here is what I did (basicly I
need to load plyr first and make sure it's rev plyr_1.1):

> library(plyr,lib.loc="~/R/myRLib")

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.11.0 (2010-04-22)
i386-pc-solaris2.10

locale:
[1] /en_US.ISO8859-1/C/en_US.ISO8859-1/en_US.ISO8859-1/C/C

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods
base

other attached packages:
[1] plyr_1.1

> library(ggplot2,lib.loc="~/R/myRLib")
Loading required package: reshape
Loading required package: grid
Loading required package: proto

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.11.0 (2010-04-22)
i386-pc-solaris2.10

locale:
[1] /en_US.ISO8859-1/C/en_US.ISO8859-1/en_US.ISO8859-1/C/C

attached base packages:

[1] grid stats graphics grDevices utils datasets
methods
[8] base

other attached packages:
[1] ggplot2_0.8.8 proto_0.3-8 reshape_0.8.3 plyr_1.1
> qplot(rnorm(20),rnorm(20)) #I now can see the plot
>


However, if I start R2.11.0 and immediately load ggplot2 from the
library location ~R/myRLib, its going to complain proto is not there
and load a older version of plyr (from a public library location with
the R installation):

> library(ggplot2,lib.loc="~/R/myRLib")
Loading required package: reshape
Loading required package: plyr

Loading required package: grid
Loading required package: proto
Error: package 'proto' could not be loaded
In addition: Warning message:
In library(pkg, character.only = TRUE, logical.return = TRUE, lib.loc
= lib.loc) :
there is no package called 'proto'
> library(proto,lib.loc="~/R/myRLib")
> library(ggplot2,lib.loc="~/R/myRLib")

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.11.0 (2010-04-22)
i386-pc-solaris2.10

locale:
[1] /en_US.ISO8859-1/C/en_US.ISO8859-1/en_US.ISO8859-1/C/C

attached base packages:

[1] grid stats graphics grDevices utils datasets
methods
[8] base

other attached packages:
[1] ggplot2_0.8.8 proto_0.3-8 reshape_0.8.3 plyr_0.1.9
>

Hence I have to first use .libPaths("~/R/myRLib") to force every
library ggplot2 depends on are loaded from the specified library
location.

Thanks, my problem resolved now.
